```{r}
# ==============================================================
# α-DIVERSITY GLMM REANALYSIS
# HOUSE RETAINED + HOUSE ICC
#
# Complete analysis from top to bottom.
#
# Does NOT overwrite previous analysis objects.
#
# Growout-specific models:
#   Response ~ Treatment + Position + (1 | House)
#
# Global models:
#   Response ~ Treatment * Growout + Position + (1 | House)
#
# House is ALWAYS retained regardless of estimated variance.
#
# Previously selected distributions are used.
# Distribution screening is NOT repeated.
#
# House variability is reported as:
#   - random-intercept variance
#   - random-intercept SD
#   - adjusted ICC
#   - unadjusted ICC
#   - adjusted ICC as %
#   - unadjusted ICC as %
#
# Excel output:
#   ONE workbook
#   ONE worksheet
#   ONE flat results table
# ==============================================================


# ==============================================================
# 0. Packages
# ==============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(glmmTMB)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
library(DHARMa)
library(performance)
library(writexl)


# ==============================================================
# 1. Check required columns
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_required <- c(
  "Sample",
  "Growout",
  "Treatment",
  "House",
  "Position",
  "Observed",
  "Shannon",
  "InvSimpson",
  "Faith_PD"
)

alpha_house_icc_missing <- setdiff(
  alpha_house_icc_required,
  names(alpha_diversity_meta)
)

if (length(alpha_house_icc_missing) > 0) {
  stop(
    "alpha_diversity_meta is missing required columns: ",
    paste(alpha_house_icc_missing, collapse = ", ")
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 2. Prepare analysis dataframe
#
# Original alpha_diversity_meta is NOT modified.
# Only Growouts 1 and 2 are included.
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_df <- alpha_diversity_meta %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    as.character(Growout) %in% c("1", "2")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Growout = factor(Growout),
    Treatment = factor(Treatment),
    House = factor(House),
    Position = factor(Position)
  )


# ==============================================================
# 3. Previously selected distributions
#
# Using simple lookup tables rather than nested list indexing.
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_pergo_lookup <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    "Observed",
    "Observed",
    "Shannon",
    "Shannon",
    "InvSimpson",
    "InvSimpson",
    "Faith_PD",
    "Faith_PD"
  ),
  Growout = c(
    "1", "2",
    "1", "2",
    "1", "2",
    "1", "2"
  ),
  Family = c(
    "gamma",
    "normal",
    "gamma",
    "normal",
    "lognorm",
    "gamma",
    "gamma",
    "gamma"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


alpha_house_icc_global_lookup <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    "Observed",
    "Shannon",
    "InvSimpson",
    "Faith_PD"
  ),
  Family = c(
    "normal",
    "gamma",
    "lognorm",
    "gamma"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


# ==============================================================
# 4. Helper: model family
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_get_family <- function(family_name) {

  if (family_name == "normal") {
    return(
      stats::gaussian(link = "identity")
    )
  }

  if (family_name == "gamma") {
    return(
      stats::Gamma(link = "log")
    )
  }

  if (family_name == "lognorm") {
    # Response is log-transformed before fitting
    return(
      stats::gaussian(link = "identity")
    )
  }

  stop(
    "Unsupported family: ",
    family_name
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 5. Helper: apply sum-to-zero contrasts
#
# Required for Type III tests.
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_set_contrasts <- function(df, variables) {

  for (v in variables) {

    if (
      is.factor(df[[v]]) &&
      nlevels(df[[v]]) > 1
    ) {

      contrasts(df[[v]]) <- contr.sum(
        nlevels(df[[v]])
      )
    }
  }

  return(df)
}


# ==============================================================
# 6. Helper: House variance and SD
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_get_variance <- function(model) {

  vc <- glmmTMB::VarCorr(model)$cond

  house_variance <- as.numeric(
    vc$House[1, 1]
  )

  house_sd <- sqrt(
    house_variance
  )

  return(
    data.frame(
      Variance = house_variance,
      SD = house_sd
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 7. Helper: House ICC
#
# performance::icc() is used because models include Gaussian,
# Gamma, and lognormal specifications.
#
# Adjusted ICC:
#   proportion of residual/model variance attributable to House
#   after accounting for the fixed effects.
#
# Unadjusted ICC:
#   proportion of overall modeled variance attributable to House,
#   including variance explained by fixed effects.
#
# tolerance = 0 keeps very small random-effect estimates rather
# than automatically discarding them as singular.
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_get_icc <- function(model) {

  icc_result <- suppressWarnings(
    tryCatch(
      performance::icc(
        model,
        tolerance = 0,
        approximation = "lognormal"
      ),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
  )

  if (is.null(icc_result)) {

    return(
      data.frame(
        ICC_adjusted = NA_real_,
        ICC_unadjusted = NA_real_,
        Percent_House_adjusted = NA_real_,
        Percent_House_unadjusted = NA_real_
      )
    )
  }

  icc_adjusted <- tryCatch(
    as.numeric(
      icc_result$ICC_adjusted[1]
    ),
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )

  icc_unadjusted <- tryCatch(
    as.numeric(
      icc_result$ICC_unadjusted[1]
    ),
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )

  return(
    data.frame(
      ICC_adjusted = icc_adjusted,
      ICC_unadjusted = icc_unadjusted,
      Percent_House_adjusted =
        icc_adjusted * 100,
      Percent_House_unadjusted =
        icc_unadjusted * 100
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 8. Helper: DHARMa p-value
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_get_dharma_p <- function(test_object) {

  if (
    is.null(test_object) ||
    is.null(test_object$p.value)
  ) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  return(
    as.numeric(
      test_object$p.value[1]
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 9. Helper: emmeans test statistic
#
# emmeans may return either t.ratio or z.ratio.
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_get_emm_stat <- function(df) {

  if ("t.ratio" %in% names(df)) {
    return(
      as.numeric(df$t.ratio)
    )
  }

  if ("z.ratio" %in% names(df)) {
    return(
      as.numeric(df$z.ratio)
    )
  }

  return(
    rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(df)
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 10. Fit ONE growout-specific model
#
# Response ~ Treatment + Position + (1 | House)
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_fit_pergo <- function(
  metric,
  growout,
  family_name,
  n_sims = 1000
) {

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Subset
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  df <- alpha_house_icc_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      as.character(Growout) == growout
    ) %>%
    droplevels()


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Contrasts
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  df <- alpha_house_icc_set_contrasts(
    df,
    c(
      "Treatment",
      "Position"
    )
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Response
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  response_var <- metric
  transform_name <- "none"

  if (family_name == "lognorm") {

    if (any(df[[metric]] <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      stop(
        metric,
        " contains non-positive values and cannot be log-transformed."
      )
    }

    response_var <- paste0(
      "log_",
      metric,
      "_house_icc"
    )

    df[[response_var]] <- log(
      df[[metric]]
    )

    transform_name <- "log"
  }


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Formula
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  model_formula <- stats::as.formula(
    paste0(
      response_var,
      " ~ Treatment + Position + (1 | House)"
    )
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
    formula = model_formula,
    family = alpha_house_icc_get_family(
      family_name
    ),
    data = df
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Type III fixed effects
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  anova3 <- car::Anova(
    model,
    type = 3
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Treatment comparison
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  emm <- emmeans::emmeans(
    model,
    ~ Treatment
  )

  pairs <- emmeans::contrast(
    emm,
    method = "pairwise",
    adjust = "BH"
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # DHARMa
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  sim <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(
    fittedModel = model,
    n = n_sims
  )

  dispersion <- DHARMa::testDispersion(
    sim
  )

  outliers <- DHARMa::testOutliers(
    sim
  )

  quantiles <- DHARMa::testQuantiles(
    sim
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # House variance
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  variance_result <- alpha_house_icc_get_variance(
    model
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # House ICC
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  icc_result <- alpha_house_icc_get_icc(
    model
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Return
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  return(
    list(
      metric = metric,
      growout = growout,
      family = family_name,
      transform = transform_name,
      n = stats::nobs(model),
      model = model,
      anova3 = anova3,
      pairs = pairs,
      variance = variance_result,
      icc = icc_result,
      dharma = list(
        sim = sim,
        dispersion = dispersion,
        outliers = outliers,
        quantiles = quantiles
      )
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 11. Fit ALL growout-specific models
#
# No nested indexing is used here.
# ==============================================================

set.seed(5080)

alpha_house_icc_models_pergo <- list()

for (
  i in seq_len(
    nrow(alpha_house_icc_pergo_lookup)
  )
) {

  metric <- alpha_house_icc_pergo_lookup$Metric[i]

  growout <- alpha_house_icc_pergo_lookup$Growout[i]

  family_name <- alpha_house_icc_pergo_lookup$Family[i]

  model_name <- paste0(
    metric,
    "_G",
    growout
  )

  cat(
    "\n========================================\n",
    model_name,
    " | ",
    family_name,
    " | random = (1 | House)\n",
    "========================================\n",
    sep = ""
  )

  alpha_house_icc_models_pergo[[model_name]] <-
    alpha_house_icc_fit_pergo(
      metric = metric,
      growout = growout,
      family_name = family_name,
      n_sims = 1000
    )
}


# ==============================================================
# 12. Fit ONE global model
#
# Response ~ Treatment * Growout + Position + (1 | House)
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_fit_global <- function(
  metric,
  family_name,
  n_sims = 1000
) {

  df <- alpha_house_icc_df


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Contrasts
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  df <- alpha_house_icc_set_contrasts(
    df,
    c(
      "Treatment",
      "Growout",
      "Position"
    )
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Response
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  response_var <- metric
  transform_name <- "none"

  if (family_name == "lognorm") {

    if (any(df[[metric]] <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      stop(
        metric,
        " contains non-positive values and cannot be log-transformed."
      )
    }

    response_var <- paste0(
      "log_",
      metric,
      "_global_house_icc"
    )

    df[[response_var]] <- log(
      df[[metric]]
    )

    transform_name <- "log"
  }


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Formula
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  model_formula <- stats::as.formula(
    paste0(
      response_var,
      " ~ Treatment * Growout + Position + (1 | House)"
    )
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
    formula = model_formula,
    family = alpha_house_icc_get_family(
      family_name
    ),
    data = df
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Type III fixed effects
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  anova3 <- car::Anova(
    model,
    type = 3
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Treatment within Growout
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  emm <- emmeans::emmeans(
    model,
    ~ Treatment | Growout
  )

  pairs <- emmeans::contrast(
    emm,
    method = "pairwise",
    adjust = "BH"
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # DHARMa
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  sim <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(
    fittedModel = model,
    n = n_sims
  )

  dispersion <- DHARMa::testDispersion(
    sim
  )

  outliers <- DHARMa::testOutliers(
    sim
  )

  quantiles <- DHARMa::testQuantiles(
    sim
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # House variance
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  variance_result <- alpha_house_icc_get_variance(
    model
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # House ICC
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  icc_result <- alpha_house_icc_get_icc(
    model
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Return
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  return(
    list(
      metric = metric,
      family = family_name,
      transform = transform_name,
      n = stats::nobs(model),
      model = model,
      anova3 = anova3,
      pairs = pairs,
      variance = variance_result,
      icc = icc_result,
      dharma = list(
        sim = sim,
        dispersion = dispersion,
        outliers = outliers,
        quantiles = quantiles
      )
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 13. Fit ALL global models
#
# Again, no nested indexing.
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_models_global <- list()

for (
  i in seq_len(
    nrow(alpha_house_icc_global_lookup)
  )
) {

  metric <- alpha_house_icc_global_lookup$Metric[i]

  family_name <- alpha_house_icc_global_lookup$Family[i]

  cat(
    "\n========================================\n",
    "GLOBAL ",
    metric,
    " | ",
    family_name,
    " | random = (1 | House)\n",
    "========================================\n",
    sep = ""
  )

  alpha_house_icc_models_global[[metric]] <-
    alpha_house_icc_fit_global(
      metric = metric,
      family_name = family_name,
      n_sims = 1000
    )
}


# ==============================================================
# 14. Helper: convert ONE fitted model to flat result rows
#
# This produces ordinary atomic columns only.
# No list-columns are created.
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_build_rows <- function(
  x,
  analysis_label
) {

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Fixed effects
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  anova_df <- as.data.frame(
    x$anova3
  )

  anova_df$Effect <- rownames(
    anova_df
  )

  rownames(anova_df) <- NULL

  anova_df <- anova_df[
    anova_df$Effect != "(Intercept)",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  if (analysis_label == "Global") {
    fixed_growout <- rep(
      "1 + 2",
      nrow(anova_df)
    )
  } else {
    fixed_growout <- rep(
      x$growout,
      nrow(anova_df)
    )
  }

  fixed_rows <- data.frame(
    Analysis = rep(
      analysis_label,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    Metric = rep(
      x$metric,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    Growout = fixed_growout,
    Family = rep(
      x$family,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    Transform = rep(
      x$transform,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    N = rep(
      x$n,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    Result_type = rep(
      "Fixed effect - Type III Wald",
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    Effect_or_contrast =
      as.character(anova_df$Effect),
    Estimate = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    SE = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    df =
      as.numeric(anova_df$Df),
    Test_statistic =
      as.numeric(anova_df$Chisq),
    P_value =
      as.numeric(
        anova_df[["Pr(>Chisq)"]]
      ),
    Variance = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    SD = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    ICC_adjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    ICC_unadjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    Percent_House_adjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    Percent_House_unadjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(anova_df)
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # emmeans treatment contrasts
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  pair_df <- as.data.frame(
    summary(x$pairs)
  )

  if (analysis_label == "Global") {

    pair_growout <- as.character(
      pair_df$Growout
    )

  } else {

    pair_growout <- rep(
      x$growout,
      nrow(pair_df)
    )
  }

  pair_rows <- data.frame(
    Analysis = rep(
      analysis_label,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    Metric = rep(
      x$metric,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    Growout = pair_growout,
    Family = rep(
      x$family,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    Transform = rep(
      x$transform,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    N = rep(
      x$n,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    Result_type = rep(
      "Treatment contrast - emmeans",
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    Effect_or_contrast =
      as.character(pair_df$contrast),
    Estimate =
      as.numeric(pair_df$estimate),
    SE =
      as.numeric(pair_df$SE),
    df =
      if ("df" %in% names(pair_df)) {
        as.numeric(pair_df$df)
      } else {
        rep(
          NA_real_,
          nrow(pair_df)
        )
      },
    Test_statistic =
      alpha_house_icc_get_emm_stat(
        pair_df
      ),
    P_value =
      as.numeric(pair_df$p.value),
    Variance = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    SD = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    ICC_adjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    ICC_unadjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    Percent_House_adjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    Percent_House_unadjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      nrow(pair_df)
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Random effect + ICC
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  if (analysis_label == "Global") {
    random_growout <- "1 + 2"
  } else {
    random_growout <- x$growout
  }

  random_row <- data.frame(
    Analysis = analysis_label,
    Metric = x$metric,
    Growout = random_growout,
    Family = x$family,
    Transform = x$transform,
    N = x$n,
    Result_type = "Random effect",
    Effect_or_contrast = "House",
    Estimate = NA_real_,
    SE = NA_real_,
    df = NA_real_,
    Test_statistic = NA_real_,
    P_value = NA_real_,
    Variance =
      as.numeric(
        x$variance$Variance[1]
      ),
    SD =
      as.numeric(
        x$variance$SD[1]
      ),
    ICC_adjusted =
      as.numeric(
        x$icc$ICC_adjusted[1]
      ),
    ICC_unadjusted =
      as.numeric(
        x$icc$ICC_unadjusted[1]
      ),
    Percent_House_adjusted =
      as.numeric(
        x$icc$Percent_House_adjusted[1]
      ),
    Percent_House_unadjusted =
      as.numeric(
        x$icc$Percent_House_unadjusted[1]
      ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # DHARMa diagnostics
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  diagnostic_rows <- data.frame(
    Analysis = rep(
      analysis_label,
      3
    ),
    Metric = rep(
      x$metric,
      3
    ),
    Growout = rep(
      random_growout,
      3
    ),
    Family = rep(
      x$family,
      3
    ),
    Transform = rep(
      x$transform,
      3
    ),
    N = rep(
      x$n,
      3
    ),
    Result_type = rep(
      "DHARMa diagnostic",
      3
    ),
    Effect_or_contrast = c(
      "Dispersion",
      "Outliers",
      "Quantiles"
    ),
    Estimate = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    SE = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    df = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    Test_statistic = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    P_value = c(
      alpha_house_icc_get_dharma_p(
        x$dharma$dispersion
      ),
      alpha_house_icc_get_dharma_p(
        x$dharma$outliers
      ),
      alpha_house_icc_get_dharma_p(
        x$dharma$quantiles
      )
    ),
    Variance = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    SD = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    ICC_adjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    ICC_unadjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    Percent_House_adjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    Percent_House_unadjusted = rep(
      NA_real_,
      3
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Combine
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  return(
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      fixed_rows,
      pair_rows,
      random_row,
      diagnostic_rows
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 15. Build growout-specific result table
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_results_pergo <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(
    alpha_house_icc_models_pergo,
    function(x) {

      alpha_house_icc_build_rows(
        x = x,
        analysis_label = "Growout-specific"
      )
    }
  )
)


# ==============================================================
# 16. Build global result table
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_results_global <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(
    alpha_house_icc_models_global,
    function(x) {

      alpha_house_icc_build_rows(
        x = x,
        analysis_label = "Global"
      )
    }
  )
)


# ==============================================================
# 17. Combine ALL results
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  alpha_house_icc_results_pergo,
  alpha_house_icc_results_global
)


# ==============================================================
# 18. Order rows for readability
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_results <- alpha_house_icc_results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Analysis_order = ifelse(
      Analysis == "Growout-specific",
      1,
      2
    ),

    Metric_order = match(
      Metric,
      c(
        "Observed",
        "Shannon",
        "InvSimpson",
        "Faith_PD"
      )
    ),

    Result_order = match(
      Result_type,
      c(
        "Fixed effect - Type III Wald",
        "Treatment contrast - emmeans",
        "Random effect",
        "DHARMa diagnostic"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    Analysis_order,
    Metric_order,
    Growout,
    Result_order
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    -Analysis_order,
    -Metric_order,
    -Result_order
  )


# ==============================================================
# 19. Confirm output is completely flat
#
# Stops before Excel export if any list-column somehow exists.
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_list_columns <- names(
  alpha_house_icc_results
)[
  vapply(
    alpha_house_icc_results,
    is.list,
    logical(1)
  )
]

if (length(alpha_house_icc_list_columns) > 0) {

  stop(
    "List-columns remain: ",
    paste(
      alpha_house_icc_list_columns,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 20. Print complete results
# ==============================================================

print(
  alpha_house_icc_results,
  n = Inf
)


# ==============================================================
# 21. Print House variance + ICC summary
#
# This is the table most directly relevant to the reviewer's
# question about magnitude of between-house variability.
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_summary <- alpha_house_icc_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Result_type == "Random effect"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Analysis,
    Metric,
    Growout,
    Family,
    Variance,
    SD,
    ICC_adjusted,
    ICC_unadjusted,
    Percent_House_adjusted,
    Percent_House_unadjusted
  )

cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "HOUSE RANDOM-EFFECT VARIANCE AND ICC\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  alpha_house_icc_summary,
  n = Inf
)


# ==============================================================
# 22. Print global fixed effects
# ==============================================================

cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "GLOBAL FIXED-EFFECT TESTS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  alpha_house_icc_results %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Analysis == "Global",
      Result_type == "Fixed effect - Type III Wald"
    ),
  n = Inf
)


# ==============================================================
# 23. Print global Treatment contrasts within Growout
# ==============================================================

cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "GLOBAL TREATMENT CONTRASTS WITHIN GROWOUT\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  alpha_house_icc_results %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Analysis == "Global",
      Result_type == "Treatment contrast - emmeans"
    ),
  n = Inf
)


# ==============================================================
# 24. Print DHARMa diagnostics
# ==============================================================

cat(
  "\n\n============================================================\n",
  "DHARMa DIAGNOSTICS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)

print(
  alpha_house_icc_results %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Result_type == "DHARMa diagnostic"
    ),
  n = Inf
)


# ==============================================================
# 25. Plot DHARMa diagnostics
# ==============================================================

invisible(
  lapply(
    alpha_house_icc_models_pergo,
    function(x) {

      plot(
        x$dharma$sim,
        main = paste0(
          x$metric,
          " - Growout ",
          x$growout
        )
      )
    }
  )
)

invisible(
  lapply(
    alpha_house_icc_models_global,
    function(x) {

      plot(
        x$dharma$sim,
        main = paste0(
          x$metric,
          " - Global"
        )
      )
    }
  )
)


# ==============================================================
# 26. Save ONE flat table to ONE Excel worksheet
# ==============================================================

alpha_house_icc_excel_file <-
  "Alpha Diversity GLMM Summary - House Retained with ICC.xlsx"

writexl::write_xlsx(
  list(
    "Alpha GLMM Results" = alpha_house_icc_results
  ),
  path = alpha_house_icc_excel_file
)


# ==============================================================
# 27. Confirm saved file
# ==============================================================

cat(
  "\nExcel file written to:\n",
  normalizePath(
    alpha_house_icc_excel_file,
    mustWork = FALSE
  ),
  "\n"
)
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================
# UPDATED ALPHA-DIVERSITY FIGURE
#
# Pairwise Treatment p-values come from the revised GLOBAL models:
#   Response ~ Treatment * Growout + Position + (1 | House)
#
# Uses final formatting from the previous figure:
#   - p-value position = 1.10 x maximum
#   - expanded upper y-axis margin
#   - width = 7.5 in
#
# Does NOT overwrite previous plotting objects.
# ==============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)


# ==============================================================
# 1. Helper to format p-values for plotmath
# ==============================================================

fmt_p_parse_house_icc <- function(p) {

  if (is.na(p)) {
    return("italic(p)==NA")
  }

  if (p < 1e-3) {
    return(
      sprintf(
        "italic(p)==%s",
        formatC(
          p,
          format = "e",
          digits = 3
        )
      )
    )
  }

  return(
    sprintf(
      "italic(p)==%.3f",
      p
    )
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 2. Build long plotting dataframe
# ==============================================================

alpha_long_plot_house_icc <- alpha_diversity_meta %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    as.character(Growout) %in% c("1", "2")
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      Observed,
      Shannon,
      InvSimpson,
      Faith_PD
    ),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Metric = dplyr::case_when(
      Metric %in% c(
        "Faith_PD",
        "Faith’s PD",
        "Faith's PD"
      ) ~ "Faith’s PD",
      TRUE ~ Metric
    ),

    Growout = as.character(
      Growout
    ),

    Treatment = factor(
      Treatment
    )
  )


# ==============================================================
# 3. Extract pairwise Treatment p-values
#
# Uses revised global models with House retained.
# ==============================================================

alpha_pairs_df_house_icc <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  alpha_house_icc_models_global,
  function(one_model, metric_name) {

    pair_df <- as.data.frame(
      summary(
        one_model$pairs
      )
    )

    keep <- grepl(
      "Control\\s*-\\s*IndigoLT|IndigoLT\\s*-\\s*Control",
      pair_df$contrast
    )

    pair_df <- pair_df[
      keep,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    if (nrow(pair_df) == 0) {

      return(
        tibble::tibble(
          Metric = character(),
          Growout = character(),
          P_Value = numeric()
        )
      )
    }

    return(
      tibble::tibble(
        Metric = metric_name,
        Growout = as.character(
          pair_df$Growout
        ),
        P_Value = as.numeric(
          pair_df$p.value
        )
      )
    )
  }
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Metric = dplyr::case_when(
      Metric %in% c(
        "Faith_PD",
        "Faith’s PD",
        "Faith's PD"
      ) ~ "Faith’s PD",
      TRUE ~ Metric
    ),

    Growout = as.character(
      Growout
    ),

    P_Label = vapply(
      P_Value,
      fmt_p_parse_house_icc,
      character(1)
    )
  )


# ==============================================================
# 4. Print p-values used in figure
# ==============================================================

print(
  alpha_pairs_df_house_icc,
  n = Inf
)


# ==============================================================
# 5. Calculate y-positions for p-value text
#
# Final formatting used 1.10 x maximum.
# ==============================================================

p_ypos_df_house_icc <- alpha_long_plot_house_icc %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Metric,
    Growout
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    y_pos = max(
      Value,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) * 1.10,
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ==============================================================
# 6. Join p-values with annotation positions
# ==============================================================

alpha_pairs_annot_house_icc <- dplyr::left_join(
  alpha_pairs_df_house_icc,
  p_ypos_df_house_icc,
  by = c(
    "Metric",
    "Growout"
  )
)


# ==============================================================
# 7. Create updated figure
# ==============================================================

alpha_pair_plot_house_icc <- ggplot(
  alpha_long_plot_house_icc,
  aes(
    x = Growout,
    y = Value
  )
) +

  geom_boxplot(
    aes(
      fill = Treatment
    ),
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.9,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.9
    )
  ) +

  stat_summary(
    aes(
      fill = Treatment
    ),
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 23,
    size = 3,
    color = "white",
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.9
    ),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  geom_jitter(
    aes(
      color = Treatment
    ),
    shape = 21,
    size = 1.25,
    alpha = 0.9,
    fill = "white",
    position = position_jitterdodge(
      jitter.width = 0.1,
      dodge.width = 0.9
    ),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  geom_text(
    data = alpha_pairs_annot_house_icc,
    aes(
      x = Growout,
      y = y_pos,
      label = P_Label
    ),
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 3,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = 0
  ) +

  facet_wrap(
    ~ Metric,
    scales = "free",
    nrow = 1
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Control" = "#f8765c",
      "IndigoLT" = "#221150"
    )
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Control" = "black",
      "IndigoLT" = "black"
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.05,
        0.15
      )
    )
  ) +

  theme_bw() +

  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 12,
      color = "black"
    ),

    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),

    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 12
    ),

    strip.background = element_blank(),

    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 14
    ),

    legend.position = "top",

    panel.spacing = grid::unit(
      1,
      "lines"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    fill = "Treatment",
    x = "Growout"
  )


# ==============================================================
# 8. Display figure
# ==============================================================

print(
  alpha_pair_plot_house_icc
)


# ==============================================================
# 9. Save figure
# ==============================================================

ggsave(
  filename = "alpha_pairwise_BH_pvalues_house_retained.png",
  plot = alpha_pair_plot_house_icc,
  width = 7.5,
  height = 3,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 900
)
```

```{r}
}
```
